messages:
maria: quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: credits & quotas — a few customer scenarios we should nail down for docs. can we confirm behavior for streaming + auto-topup? :eyes:
phil: good call. what's the customer flow? auto-topup (card on file) vs strict quota?
devon: scenario: websocket stream where tokens accumulate over minutes. if a billing auto-topup occurs mid-stream, do we continue the stream or close and issue a resubmit error?
tariq: ops note: we treat token accounting continuously. if payment succeeds we allow continuation; if payment fails we mark the session and emit an `error` frame.
sophie: SDK behavior: we'll surface an error event and include `quota_state` and `billing_action` fields. example: `{"type":"error","code":"billing_required","detail":"auto-topup_failed"}`
billing-bot: current policy: if auto-topup enabled, requests will continue when payment clears. if payment fails, the session receives `quota_exhausted` and `retry_after` in seconds.
phil: product question: should we support a "soft cap" mode where streams are throttled (slower token pace) instead of full stop? some teams want degraded experience vs abrupt cut-off.
devon: we have customers who prefer graceful slowdown for UX. technically we can implement token pacing at the proxy. downside: changes perceived latency/cost.
sophie: idea: expose `quota_behavior` flag per API key: `strict` (429), `graceful` (slowdown + warning), `fallback` (route to cheaper model). SDKs would surface a `quota_warning` event.
maria: legal/compliance ask: if we fallback to a cheaper model due to credits, do we need explicit consent for model quality degradation?
phil: default: no explicit opt-in today; fallback respects customer routing policy. for enterprise customers we should require explicit consent in config to avoid surprise regressions.
billing-bot: note: current 429 payload: {"error":"quota_exceeded","retry_after":1800,"remaining_credits":0}. ops recommends keeping `retry_after` as seconds.
tariq: infra ask: if we return 429 mid-stream for SSE/WS, we should include a structured final event and close the connection cleanly. partial HTTP payload truncation is messy for clients.
devon: agree. SDKs need stable hooks: `onMessage`, `onError`, `onClose` with structured reason codes.
sophie: docs will show code examples for handling mid-stream quota errors across HTTP/WS/SSE. also add recommended backoff pattern using `Retry-After` seconds.
maria: leadership ask: can leftover promo/dev credits be gifted to other teams or converted to console credits? we got multiple asks in the Q&A.
illing-bot: policy: promo/dev credits are non-transferable and expire per terms. conversion requires sales approval and manual ledger adjustments.
phil: product follow-up: we should evaluate self-serve conversions (guardrails: max convert, 14d validity, one-time). needs billing + legal signoff.
ariq: operational concern: conversion flow must lock credit buckets while conversion is in-flight to prevent race conditions.
devon: roadmap ask: console feature to forecast credit exhaustion and recommend purchase size (confidence band, 7/30/90 day). this will reduce surprise outages.
sophie: Optimize already has a prototype; needs UX and API hooks for forecast export.
maria: actionable next steps: A) docs PR for mid-stream credit/auto-topup behavior (owner @sophie). B) spec for `quota_behavior` flag and SDK events (owner @devon). C) feasibility for self-serve conversion (owner @phil + billing). D) console forecast spike (owner @tariq).
phil: added to roadmap board. thanks all — let's reconvene Thursday 10am PT to review PRs. :thumbsup:
